name: BlueSlide
notes: Named colors are BlueSlide's house palette as used in its PowerPoint template and reference decks; #858487 is the label gray. accent_amber_text is the only derived value.

gold_accent (#FFB300) is the single accent, the complementary hue to the blues, at 9.10:1 against deep navy. It fails as text on light backgrounds (1.79:1 on white); on light slides use it as a fill, highlight bar, or marker behind navy text (navy on #FFB300 is 9.10:1), or use accent_amber_text for accent-colored words.
The cool light grays are panels, dividers, and quiet chart fills, not slide backgrounds; only navy, charcoal, and dark gray text meets 4.5:1 on them.

pptx_theme maps the palette onto PowerPoint/Google Slides theme slots so default shapes, charts, and links inherit BlueSlide colors instead of Office defaults such as #4F81BD. accent1 is the default series and shape color; accent2 is the gold accent.

Chart marks below 3:1 against their background (light blues, gold, cool grays on white) are allowed only when each mark carries a direct value label; otherwise outline them in deep navy or use a darker palette color.
Supporting blues are fills, chart series, and dark-background text only; they fail 4.5:1 as text on white.

Contrast ratios are WCAG 2.x relative-luminance ratios. House rule: require 4.5:1 for all slide text, because projectors and shared screens wash out contrast; keep non-text elements that carry meaning at 3:1 or better, except directly labeled chart marks. Verify custom colors with scripts/check_contrast.py.
Never use pure black for text or icons; use charcoal or deep navy.
